title: Lisse integral lattices on finite strata of a topologically Noetherian scheme
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $E\subseteq\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ be a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with Noetherian underlying topological space (every ascending chain of open subsets stabilizes). Use the coefficient rings $A_T=\mathcal O_{E,T}$ and $B_T=E_T$ pulled back from the condensed topological rings for every scheme $T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and the pulled-back inclusion $A_T\to B_T$ [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield]. A module means an internal module object in abelian sheaves on the small pro-étale site [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. A module over either coefficient ring is called lisse if a pro-étale cover makes it a finite direct sum of that coefficient ring; finite ranks may vary.

For every lisse $B_X$-module $L$, there is a finite stratification $X=\coprod_a S_a$ by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification] such that, on every stratum, there is a lisse $A_{S_a}$-submodule $L_{0,a}\subseteq L|_{S_a}$ whose inclusion induces an isomorphism
$$B_{S_a}\otimes_{A_{S_a}}L_{0,a}\xrightarrow{\sim}L|_{S_a}.$$
The empty scheme and rank-zero modules are included; no single lisse lattice on all of $X$ is asserted.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13, first paragraph, pp. 60–61; coefficient and lisse conventions: Definitions 6.8.1, 6.8.3 and Lemma 6.8.2

proof.text: Every open subset of a Noetherian topological space is quasi-compact: otherwise successive finite unions from an open cover without a finite subcover give a strictly increasing chain of opens. Thus $X$ is quasi-compact and its affine-open intersections are quasi-compact, so it is quasi-separated. Both $E$ and $\mathcal O_E$ are totally disconnected: two distinct points are separated by clopen ultrametric balls. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations] to identify their pulled condensed coefficient rings with the continuous-function coefficient sheaves, compatibly with the inclusion. These identifications hold on all the schemes below. Transporting an action along a ring isomorphism preserves its finite-free charts and tensor products: the same bases and bilinear maps define them after transport. By [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], internal module objects over these commutative coefficient sheaves and ordinary sheafwise module objects have the same underlying sheaves, sections, restrictions, and linear maps. Thus we may read internal module objects as ordinary module sheaves: evaluating an action gives the sectionwise scalar multiplication, and conversely a bilinear sectionwise action induces the internal action by the sheaf tensor universal property. Hence the given $L$ is a lisse module for the continuous rational coefficients.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-etale-local-lattice] to this internal rational module. Its hypotheses hold: the finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ carries its usual normed-field structure, is finite dimensional, and $X$ is topologically Noetherian. It gives a qcqs scheme $U$, an étale surjection $p:U\to X$, a pro-étale locally finite free integral module $M$, and an isomorphism $B_U\otimes_{A_U}M\simeq p^*L$. The comparison of step 1 commutes with the integral-to-rational map, so this is the scalar extension for the pulled condensed coefficient rings $A_U$ and $B_U$. Varying finite ranks, including zero, are permitted by the cited theorem.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6); Lemma 6.8.13 first paragraph, étale-cover reduction

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-stratified-finite] to $p:U\to X$; both source and target are qcqs by steps 1 and 2. It gives finitely many constructible locally closed strata $S_a$ and finite étale maps $p_a:U_a=U\times_X S_a\to S_a$. These maps are surjective. Indeed for a point $s\in S_a$ over $x\in X$, choose $u\in U$ over $x$. The nonzero tensor product $\kappa(u)\otimes_{\kappa(x)}\kappa(s)$ has a prime ideal, yielding a point in the fibre product over $s$. Each $S_a$ is topologically Noetherian: a closed subspace inherits stabilization of open chains, and an open subspace does too, since its opens are opens of the ambient space. Thus the Noetherian-space hypothesis needed for descent is retained.

Pull $M$ back to each $U_a$, obtaining $M_a$. The composite $U_a\to U\xrightarrow{p}X$ equals $U_a\xrightarrow{p_a}S_a\hookrightarrow X$, so the composition isomorphisms of module pullbacks [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] identify the pullback of $p^*L$ to $U_a$ with $p_a^*(L|_{S_a})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-locally-free-pullback], both $M_a$ and $L|_{S_a}$ remain locally finite free, with ranks allowed to vary. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1), the inverse images of both coefficient rings identify with the coefficient rings on the new scheme; the module pullback is the lift of ordinary sheaf inverse image. The definition of module pullback [def-sfb-module-upper-star], together with the strong monoidal inverse-image structure [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal], identifies the pulled scalar-extension object with $B_{U_a}\otimes_{A_{U_a}}M_a$. The scalar-extension isomorphism therefore pulls back to $B_{U_a}\otimes_{A_{U_a}}M_a\simeq p_a^{-1}(L|_{S_a})$. To check this compatibility explicitly, on a chart $M\simeq A_U^r$ use the basis $e_i$. Scalar extension has basis $1\otimes e_i$, and pulling back yields the corresponding bases over $A_{U_a}$ and $B_{U_a}$. The matrices for the original rational isomorphism and its inverse pull back to matrices whose products are still the identity. Thus the pulled map is an isomorphism on these charts. These maps agree on overlaps, since they come from the same original map, and their inverses glue by the sheaf axiom.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13 first paragraph, restriction to strata; inverse-image coefficient identifications

proof.text: Fix a nonempty stratum $S_a$. The field $E$ is finite over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, $S_a$ is topologically Noetherian, $p_a$ is finite étale surjective, $L|_{S_a}$ is lisse, and $M_a$ is a lisse integral model of its inverse image. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-finite-etale-descent] supplies a lisse integral module $N_a$ and an isomorphism $\theta_a:B_{S_a}\otimes_{A_{S_a}}N_a\simeq L|_{S_a}$. Its statement requires no descent datum on $M_a$, so none has been assumed here. The descent theorem is stated for sectionwise module sheaves over the continuous-function rings, so pass through the specified encoding [def-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-module-encoding], the equivalence assembled from the two identifications of step 1. It sends regular modules to unit sheaves, finite biproducts to free sheaves, and commutes with restriction of scalars, hence with its left adjoint, extension of scalars. Its compatibility with restriction to slices [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-module-encoding-slice-freeness] shows that the encoded $M_a$ and $L|_{S_a}$ are locally free of finite rank. By [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-module-encoding-restriction] for the étale map $p_a$, the encoding of $p_a^*(L|_{S_a})$ is the inverse image of the encoding of $L|_{S_a}$, so the isomorphism of step 4 becomes the hypothesis of the descent theorem. Conversely, [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-module-encoding-lattices], applied to the identity of $S_a$ and the integral module sheaf $N_a$ with its rationalization isomorphism, makes the inverse encoding of $N_a$ a pro-étale locally finite free internal integral module whose ordinary scalar extension is isomorphic to $L|_{S_a}$. Write $N_a$ and $\theta_a$ again for this internal module and isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13 first paragraph, finite étale descent

proof.text: The map $n\mapsto\theta_a(1\otimes n)$ is injective. On a pro-étale cover trivializing $N_a\simeq A_{S_a}^r$, the map before $\theta_a$ is the coordinatewise inclusion $A_{S_a}^r\to B_{S_a}^r$. This is injective because $C(V,\mathcal O_E)\to C(V,E)$ is injective for every $V$. If two sections have equal images, their restrictions to this cover are equal; the sheaf uniqueness axiom then makes them equal. Define $L_{0,a}$ as the image submodule. The injective map identifies it with $N_a$, so it is lisse. Its inclusion induces precisely $\theta_a$ under this identification, hence becomes the required isomorphism after scalar extension. Do this for the finitely many nonempty strata and discard empty ones. For $X=\varnothing$ use the empty partition; the same coordinate calculation with $r=0$ includes rank-zero modules.
